questions.q: At what level does the article say spirituality begins?
options: The level of withdrawal from society
Not quite. The article says: The level of the mind – through reflection on who we are and the purpose of life.
The level of the mind – through reflection on who we are and the purpose of life
Yes. It is an intellectual process before it shapes the personality.
The level of custom and dress
Not quite. The article says: The level of the mind – through reflection on who we are and the purpose of life.
The level of bodily exercise
Not quite. The article says: The level of the mind – through reflection on who we are and the purpose of life.
questions.rationale: “Spirituality begins at the level of the mind. It is based on reflection and contemplation, and is therefore an intellectual process.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, do people take good health for granted?
options: Because illness is very rare
Not quite. The article says: It comes without visible effort on their part, so they assume it is theirs by right.
Because health does not matter much
Not quite. The article says: It comes without visible effort on their part, so they assume it is theirs by right.
Because doctors can cure everything
Not quite. The article says: It comes without visible effort on their part, so they assume it is theirs by right.
It comes without visible effort on their part, so they assume it is theirs by right
Right. In fact the body is a trust from the Creator.
questions.rationale: “Because this gift is given without any visible effort on our part, we begin to assume that it is our inherent right.”

questions.q: How does the article regard thinking about death?
options: As a cause of despair
Not quite. The article says: As realism, not pessimism – it brings balance, humility and gratitude.
As something only for the old
Not quite. The article says: As realism, not pessimism – it brings balance, humility and gratitude.
As a harmful habit
Not quite. The article says: As realism, not pessimism – it brings balance, humility and gratitude.
As realism, not pessimism – it brings balance, humility and gratitude
Yes. Those conscious of death understand life.
questions.rationale: “To think about death is not pessimism; it is realism. It brings balance to life. It prevents arrogance and fosters humility.”

questions.q: If parents speak harshly, how should their children respond, according to the article?
options: By reducing their care
Not quite. The article says: Still gently and with respect – the duty rests on a moral principle, not on the parents’ behaviour.
Still gently and with respect – the duty rests on a moral principle, not on the parents’ behaviour
Well read. It is a test of character.
By keeping away from them
Not quite. The article says: Still gently and with respect – the duty rests on a moral principle, not on the parents’ behaviour.
In the same tone
Not quite. The article says: Still gently and with respect – the duty rests on a moral principle, not on the parents’ behaviour.
questions.rationale: “This is because the command is not based on the behaviour of the parents, but on a higher moral principle.”

questions.q: Pressed to say whether he was an atheist, how did Einstein describe himself in the letter quoted?
options: As a firm atheist
Not quite. The article says: As an agnostic, who did not share “the crusading spirit of the professional atheist”.
As having no interest in the question
Not quite. The article says: As an agnostic, who did not share “the crusading spirit of the professional atheist”.
As a devout believer
Not quite. The article says: As an agnostic, who did not share “the crusading spirit of the professional atheist”.
As an agnostic, who did not share “the crusading spirit of the professional atheist”
Correct. Neither a denier nor a conventional believer.
questions.rationale: “You may call me an agnostic, but I do not share the crusading spirit of the professional atheist.”

questions.q: Scientists accept electrons and quarks though no one has seen them. How does the article apply this to belief in God?
options: Belief needs no reasoning
Not quite. The article says: What is not seen directly can reasonably be accepted through its effects and its fit with what is observed.
Particles do not really exist
Not quite. The article says: What is not seen directly can reasonably be accepted through its effects and its fit with what is observed.
Nothing unseen should be accepted
Not quite. The article says: What is not seen directly can reasonably be accepted through its effects and its fit with what is observed.
What is not seen directly can reasonably be accepted through its effects and its fit with what is observed
Yes. Science gives indirect support, not laboratory proof.
questions.rationale: “Scientists accept their existence because their effects can be measured and studied. The same logic can be extended further.”

questions.q: A dispute in Baghdad over the meaning of a verse ended in bloodshed. What does the article say needs to be rejected in such cases?
options: Every difference of opinion
Not quite. The article says: Excess and extremism – not disagreement itself, which is to be conducted by reasoning.
All discussion of religion
Not quite. The article says: Excess and extremism – not disagreement itself, which is to be conducted by reasoning.
The study of history
Not quite. The article says: Excess and extremism – not disagreement itself, which is to be conducted by reasoning.
Excess and extremism – not disagreement itself, which is to be conducted by reasoning
Right. Unity is built on tolerating difference.
questions.rationale: “What deserves rejection in such situations is not disagreement itself, but excess and extremism.”

questions.q: What does the article say awakens the dormant potential in ordinary people?
options: A meaningful mission – purpose and challenge, not comfort and routine
Yes. As in the effort to reach the moon.
Higher pay
Not quite. The article says: A meaningful mission – purpose and challenge, not comfort and routine.
Longer holidays
Not quite. The article says: A meaningful mission – purpose and challenge, not comfort and routine.
Strict supervision
Not quite. The article says: A meaningful mission – purpose and challenge, not comfort and routine.
questions.rationale: “What awakens this potential is not comfort, but challenge; not routine, but purpose. A great mission gives direction to one’s energies.”

questions.q: On what does the article say the smooth working of a family, like any system, equally depends?
options: One member deciding everything
Not quite. The article says: The fulfilment of duties with mutual understanding and cooperation, not only the claiming of rights.
Each member acting independently
Not quite. The article says: The fulfilment of duties with mutual understanding and cooperation, not only the claiming of rights.
Avoiding relatives
Not quite. The article says: The fulfilment of duties with mutual understanding and cooperation, not only the claiming of rights.
The fulfilment of duties with mutual understanding and cooperation, not only the claiming of rights
Exactly. Each person is part of a larger whole.
questions.rationale: “Modern thinking often emphasizes individual rights, but the smooth functioning of any system depends equally on the fulfilment of responsibilities.”

questions.q: A powerful solar storm in 2012 passed without striking the Earth. What reflection does the article draw from it?
options: Technology can now stop solar storms
Not quite. The article says: Life is protected at every moment by a finely balanced system beyond human control, which calls for gratitude.
The sun is growing weaker
Not quite. The article says: Life is protected at every moment by a finely balanced system beyond human control, which calls for gratitude.
Such storms are harmless
Not quite. The article says: Life is protected at every moment by a finely balanced system beyond human control, which calls for gratitude.
Life is protected at every moment by a finely balanced system beyond human control, which calls for gratitude
Well reasoned. “Who guards you by night and by day?”
questions.rationale: “The survival of life on Earth is not merely the result of human effort or technological advancement. Rather, it depends on a complex and finely balanced system that operates far beyond human control.”
